title: Tech Layoffs Mean AI Skills Are Your Ticket In
metaDescription: Tech layoffs are making room for people who actually understand AI. The reshuffling is happening now and it's creating openings.
author: Marty @ CertFlo

sections.heading: Something's Shifting in Tech
sections.body: Business Insider is calling it an "AI air pocket" — tech layoffs picking up as companies figure out what work actually looks like now. They're asking if this is temporary or permanent. idk man, it's neither. It's a reshuffling. And reshufflings create winners. The Business Insider piece gets at something that's happening right now. Companies aren't just cutting costs. They're making room for what's coming next. The roles getting cut? Usually the ones that don't fit where work is heading. The roles being created? They need completely different people. This isn't a crisis. It's the market making space for people who see what's coming.

sections.heading: Why This Is Actually Your Opening
sections.body:
Every big workplace shift follows the same pattern. First the disruption. Then opportunity for people who moved early. Internet boom, mobile revolution, now AI automation. Same thing.

The workers getting laid off? Most are stuck in yesterday's skill set. The ones getting promoted and hired? They learned AI tools six months ago while everyone else was still debating if this was "just a fad."

Here's what the numbers miss: companies are hunting for people who can bridge traditional work and AI productivity. They need people who can actually implement AI automation, manage AI workflows, think strategically about where this stuff fits.

Not just tech people either.

sections.heading: The New Advantage Is Already Here
sections.body:
I'm watching something happen. People who started building AI skills early this year are getting opportunities that didn't exist twelve months ago. They're becoming the go-to people in their organizations. Landing roles with "AI" in the title that pay 20-40% more than traditional positions.

These aren't necessarily tech workers. Marketers using AI for content. Operations managers automating workflows. Sales people using AI for prospecting. Project managers coordinating AI-human teams.

The future isn't humans versus machines. It's AI-skilled humans versus everyone else. And right now, while everything's shifting, is exactly when you make your move.

sections.heading: Your Window Is Open

The people building AI skills now will be the ones leading teams, getting promoted, commanding premium salaries as things stabilize.
